card: Implements the BIP-348 OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK opcode in Tapscript for regtest only. Bitcoin scripts cannot currently verify Schnorr signatures over arbitrary data on the stack, limiting prototyping for oracle protocols and covenants. The PR author highlights that providing a regtest implementation allows testing and composing CSFS alongside other covenant opcodes like CTV ahead of potential soft fork bundling. No mainnet or testnet activation is included.
evidence: PR description notes that the opcode implementation allows experimentation and composition with other proposals: 'This change can be composed with other opcode specifications (e.g. CTV, see #31989) and bundled into the same deployment (yet to be specified).' Reference is made to the Delving Bitcoin thread 'ctv-csfs-can-we-reach-consensus-on-a-first-step-towards-covenants'.
problem: Tapscript cannot verify signatures over arbitrary data on the stack, preventing smart contract developers from testing covenant designs, oracle attestations, and delegated signature schemes against Bitcoin Core node consensus logic.
scope_notes: Touches consensus interpreter code to execute OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK and update validation weight accounting. Modifies XOnlyPubKey::VerifySchnorr to accept arbitrary-length message spans instead of fixed 32-byte hashes.
summary: Implements BIP-348 (OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK) in Tapscript by repurposing OP_SUCCESS204 (0xcc). The opcode enables verifying 64-byte Schnorr signatures against arbitrary messages supplied on the stack rather than transaction sighashes. Activation is restricted to regtest via an always-active BIP9 deployment, leaving consensus and policy behavior on mainnet and other networks unchanged.
